title: FUTURE · What skills must stay human?

slides.name: 1 · Teacher preparation

params.text:
Ages 11–18  ·  5 minutes  ·  no preparation, no account, no extra materials
Timing  30s scenario  ·  45s vote  ·  75s pairs  ·  75s reveal  ·  30s remember  ·  45s action
You need  this deck on the board. Phones are optional — a show of hands works.

slides.notes:
PURPOSE. Students identify one capability they will keep developing themselves. Explicitly NOT an anti-AI session — every good example on slide 5 involves using AI.

THE FRAME. EEF on metacognition: plan, monitor, evaluate. A tool that does all three for you has not helped you learn, however good the output was.

LIKELY RESPONSES. Take "nothing — I would be fine" seriously. For some students it is true, and treating it as denial teaches them not to answer honestly.

TONE. Slide 4 is the sharpest question in the campaign and needs a safe room. Pairs, not whole-class. You are not fishing for confessions.

SEND / YOUNGER LEARNERS. Reframe as "what could you still do if the internet was off for a week?" Concrete and less self-critical.

EXTENSION. For one week, write one sentence after each AI use: did that strengthen my thinking or replace it?

SOURCE. Education Endowment Foundation, metacognition and self-regulation.

slides.name: 2 · What skills must stay human?
slides.notes:
SLIDE 1 · TITLE. Up as the class comes in. The question does the work; do not explain it yet.

The full teacher page is the hidden slide before this one — purpose, timing, script, safeguarding, SEND and an extension.

slides.name: 3 · quote

params.text: Tomorrow the tool you use most is switched off. The work is still due.

slides.notes:
BEAT 1 · 30 SECONDS.

Not a threat and not a prediction. A thought experiment that makes the dependency visible, which is the only way to measure it.

slides.name: 4 · What would you struggle with most?

params.text: What would you struggle with most?
Without something to check it for you.
It only ever saved you time.
Choose A, B, C or D. Be ready to say why.

slides.notes:
BEAT 2 · 45 SECONDS. Vote first, and make it anonymous in feel — this is the one question in the campaign where students are reporting on themselves.

Take the fourth option seriously. For some of them it is true, and treating it as denial teaches them not to answer honestly.

feedback.prompt: What would you struggle with most?

slides.name: 5 · statement

params.text: Which part of your thinking have you quietly stopped practising?

slides.notes:
BEAT 3 · 75 SECONDS. The sharpest question in the campaign, and the one that needs the safest room. Pairs, not the whole class.

You are not fishing for confessions. You are making the difference between using a tool and outsourcing a skill something they can feel.

slides.name: 6 · Strengthening, or replacing?

params.text: You draft, then ask it to argue back
You decide, it checks your reasoning
It gives you options, you choose
It gives you one answer, you take it
You could not explain any of it
You got faster at avoiding it
Frame after the EEF on metacognition — plan, monitor, evaluate your own learning

slides.notes:
BEAT 4 · 75 SECONDS. Reveal a row at a time.

NOT AN ANTI-AI SLIDE, and it will be misread as one if you let it. Every left-hand row involves using AI. The difference is where the thinking happened.

Row 4 is the usable test, because it works during the task rather than afterwards: could you explain this choice to someone who asked?

The EEF frame, if you want it: plan, monitor, evaluate. A tool that does all three for you has not helped you learn, however good the output was.

slides.name: 7 · What to remember

params.text: If you could not explain it, it was not you.
Keep practising what you would miss
Pick the skill, not the task.
Ask it to challenge your work, not to produce it.
Three things, in the order you would use them

slides.notes:
SLIDE 6 · 30 SECONDS. Reveal one at a time. Three is the limit — a fourth rule is a rule nobody remembers.

Numbered rather than bulleted so the order is part of the message, and so nothing here depends on colour to be understood.

slides.name: 8 · Pick one thing you will keep doing yourself

params.text: Pick one thing you will keep doing yourself
Choose one part of your thinking you will keep practising, even when something could do it faster.

slides.notes:
BEAT 5 · 45 SECONDS.

Ask for one, not a list. A list is a wish; one is a decision.

Close the campaign on the line it is built around: AI can answer, create, recommend and increasingly act for you. Your job is deciding when to use it, when to question it, and when to keep humans in control.

slides.name: 9 · Two words worth knowing

params.text: Thinking about your own thinking — planning how you will work, noticing how it is going, and judging how it went.
Handing a mental job to something else. Useful for a shopping list. Costly for a skill you still need.

slides.notes:
HIDDEN FROM THE SHOW — the brief asks for seven student-facing slides and this is not one of them.

Worth thirty seconds anyway. Both terms are used on the slides this deck shows, and a word nobody defines is a word nobody argues with.

Written for 11–16, not for a policy paper.
